transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-21 16:00 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Marta (Redwood CSM); Liam, Priya, Evan, Sara (Helium Dynamics)

Summary: QBR style health check; discuss cost spike in Oct, two reliability incidents, consider Dedicated/reserved capacity for predictable cost, go over security docs and next steps.

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for making time for the QBR, i know schedules are tight, um quick roll call?
[00:10] Liam: hey liam here, liam o'connor, head of ml ops.
[00:15] Priya: priya menon, platform lead.
[00:18] Evan: evan brooks, cto.
[00:20] Sara: sara kim, sre.
[00:23] Daniel: daniel cho, se at redwood, will cover perf and benchmarks later.
[00:28] Marta: marta ruiz, csm, i'll own follow ups and docs.
[00:35] Aisha: quick agenda, usage & cost, reliability incidents, security, roadmap, next steps. sound ok?
[00:40] Evan: yep go ahead.

[02:05] Aisha: ok usage — we saw a 42% token increase in oct vs sept, most of that is high-variation chat sessions and some new internal batch jobs hitting embeddings, priya is that aligned with what you've seen?
[02:20] Priya: yeah we spun up an experiment for semantic search in late sept, it's heavier on embeddings, and we also had a marketing batch that wasn't rate-limited properly so that spiked calls overnight, so some ops mistake on our side.
[02:38] Aisha: cool, that explains part of it. daniel, any quick notes on cost levers we can optimize?
[02:46] Daniel: sure, so two quick things: one, batching for embeddings and prefix caching for chat can drop per-token cost significantly—our telemetry shows for Helium typical embedding workloads can see 20–40% cost reduction with smarter batching; two, quantization/model variant: if latency tolerance is ok you can move to the 8-bit quantized variant for most workloads. also worth considering dedicated reserved capacity if you want predictable per-month costs vs pay-as-you-go spikes.

[05:15] Priya: question on dedicated — if we move to dedicated reserved, does that mean we need to change our prompts or code?
[05:25] Daniel: no code changes, same api; you just pick the dedicated model variant and route. there are config knobs for autoscale, burst, and routing policy. small caveat: idle capacity incurs commit costs so you size it to baseline QPS.

[08:10] Evan: we care about tail latency—our ui is latency sensitive. can you share p95/p99 numbers?
[08:18] Daniel: prelim numbers on hosted are p95 ~ 180ms for short chats, p99 ~ 420ms for higher context lengths. with Dedicated on same hw we can tune kernels and reduce p99 by 20–30% in our tests; we'll run a tailored benchmark with your prompt set to confirm.
[09:02] Sara: we also saw two incidents in oct where requests 503'd during a nightly job, any root cause?
[09:10] Marta: from our incident review — both were capacity exhaust events on a shared pool and an upstream infra flapping with autoscaler overshoot; we've patched same-day and added better autoscaling and queueing. redwood also applied temporary fallback routing to lower-tier models which kept core product up.
[09:38] Liam: ok thanks — would dedicated have isolation so those noisy neighbors don't impact us?
[09:44] Daniel: yes, Dedicated gives capacity isolation; you'll also get SLA-backed uptime and a separate billing profile.

[11:50] Aisha: on security, hel ----------------- what are your requirements? evan?
[11:58] Evan: we need SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys, audit logs and data residency in us-east and eu-west for some customers, plus SOC2 and iso compliance docs.
[12:15] Marta: we have SSO and SAML support, we can integrate with your identity provider; KMS/HSM for optional key management is supported on Private and Dedicated tiers, and we do provide audit logs sent to customer S3 or your syslog. i'll share the SOC2/ISO artifact pack after the call.
[12:32] Priya: is the KMS option available in hosted? we prefer customer-managed keys.
[12:39] Daniel: hosted supports bring-your-own-key for encryption at rest on dedicated/private; true customer-managed KMS is available on Private deployments, and we can discuss a hybrid for dedicated — i'll detail in the security doc.

[15:00] Liam: curious about network setup — we are hybrid cloud, VPC peering required and we have strict egress rules.
[15:08] Marta: Private offering supports VPC peering and on-prem packages if you need air-gapped. for dedicated we can do private control plane plus customer-managed network circuits.

[17:22] Priya: ok back to costs — can you give an example monthly estimate if we reserve capacity for our baseline 1.2M tokens/day?
[17:32] Aisha: i'll put together a per-route cost breakdown but rough back-of-envelope — committed capacity reduces per-token unit cost ~15–25% vs hosted PAYG for steady workloads; exact depends on model choice and batching. we'll include concrete numbers in the QBR deck.

[20:05] Daniel: one more ops note — we can enable prefix KV caching to speed up repeated context; for your support chat flows where customers repeat context we often see 30–50% latency improvement. caching requires some telemetry flags but no code rewrite.

[22:40] Sara: how intrusive is the telemetry? are there pii concerns?
[22:47] Marta: we only request anonymized request logs; you can sanitize PII before transfer, and redwood supports token redaction on ingestion. we'll include guidance in the docs.

[25:10] Evan: roadmap question — any upcoming features that would help multi-tenant visibility or cost attribution per product team?
[25:20] Aisha: yes, in the console roadmap we plan token-level per-route chargebacks and per-model dashboards with alerts, rollout to production early q1-2026; also quality regression alerts tied to eval prompts. we'll share the roadmap snapshot.

[28:00] Priya: about benchmarks — what do you need from us to run the performance tests?
[28:08] Daniel: 1) representative prompt set (you mentioned you'll provide), 2) sample traffic profile (seq length distribution, QPS spikes), 3) target latency SLOs. we'll run p50/p95/p99 and throughput sweeps on a staging cluster matched to your planned Dedicated HW.

[31:15] Liam: any blockers for a pilot? cost is fine but we need enterprise terms and support SLAs.
[31:22] Aisha: we can draft an engagement that starts with a 30-day pilot on Dedicated trial nodes, include a week of benchmark and then optional commit; legal can share T&Cs and SLA addendum.

[34:40] Marta: action recap — we'll share docs, a deck, and schedule the benchmark. daniel will own the benchmark, aisha will send cost breakdown.

[36:05] Evan: one last thing — competitors, we did talk to had some pitch about an integrated data plane; how do you position vs hugging face and vertex?
[36:15] Aisha: we focus on production-first inference: predictable economics, routing/fallbacks, and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private — basically less ops burden while keeping you in control of cost and SLAs.

[38:50] Priya: timeline — if we get the docs and run the benchmark before end of nov can we aim for a pilot start early dec?
[38:58] Aisha: yes that's reasonable; we'll aim to have the benchmark week of 11-24 and pilot kickoff first week of dec.

[41:10] Daniel: i'll propose specific hardware and test matrix in an email after this, and include p99 reductions we typically observe on dedicated configurations.

[41:28] Marta: ok next steps noted.

[43:00] Aisha: thanks everyone — appreciate the time. quick recap for ease: aisha send qbr deck + cost break down by 11/25; daniel run perf bench w/ your prompt set 11/24-11/27; marta share security artifacts by 11/26; priya share logs by 11/28. any objections?
[43:25] Evan: none.
[43:28] Liam: all good.
[43:30] Priya: thanks all.
[44:00] Marta: we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and share the docs. thanks.
[44:30] Aisha: bye everyone.
